Background
The French, victorious over the Mamluks, had driven Murad Bey from the Fayoum and forced him to retreat to Upper Egypt. However, he, still master of Upper Egypt, did not consider himself defeated and continued to harass the French with his large cavalry force, waiting for an opportunity to attack them in open battle. The French, possessing only infantry, could not defend the territory they occupied against the frequent Mamluk incursions. General Desaix, who commanded in this region, informed Bonaparte of his situation and soon received reinforcements of 1,000 cavalrymen and three pieces of light artillery, commanded by General Davout, with orders to drive Murad Bey beyond the cataracts of the Nile and to exterminate the Mamluks or expel them from Egypt.
Prelude
In accordance with these orders, Davout and Desaix marched against Murad Bey, but he constantly evaded their pursuit.
On 9 Nivôse, Year VII ( December 29, 1798The French army arrived at Girga, the capital of Upper Egypt , and stopped there to await a flotilla that was to bring them munitions.
